28 ákṣata 'unhurt' RV., 'not crushed' ĀśvGr̥., m. pl. 'uncrushed barley' Kālid. [ kṣatá -¹] Pa. akkhata - 'unhurt'; Pk. akkhaya - 'unhurt, unbroken',
m. pl. 'uncrushed rice'; S. akho m. 'offering of
grain thrown into water or given to mendicants'; Ku. ã̄khat 'rice soaked in water and used for religious purposes'
(X lw. Sk.); A. ākhai 'parched paddy, husked maize'; G. ākhũ 'whole, uncastrated', ākhlɔ m. 'uncastrated bull', ākhī f. 'ceremony of carrying rice or corn in the hand
round a person to remove the effects of the evil eye';
M. ā̆khā 'whole, undivided'; Ko. ākho , āko 'complete'. Addenda: ákṣata-: S.kcch. ã̄kho m. 'bull'.
